Hello, everyone. I don't usually post aside from commenting here and there, but a few days ago I witnessed something that I felt that I should express.

It's a local business, so workplace conduct is not enforced unless it's rash and brainless swearing/vulgarities around customers, or any other basics. I like my job for what it is, so I'm not complaining.

Now, for the short story: There is an obese woman with whom I work that is in cahoots with the owner. Aside from them being too occasionally touchy or saying something about their sex life, I can deal with it; it's work.

She decides to make herself lunch, which is a chicken patty. When I see her I ask what she will use for a bun. We only have loaves of bread so that's what I asked if she was going to use that. "Bread has way too many carbs, I'm not eating that!"(no punctuation outside brackets) Being professional, I said nothing to incite anger. A moment afterwards, I see her getting some dipping sauce for her slab of breaded chicken. Nothing to write home about. She put ranch dressing in a container then mixed mostly mild hot sauce(no comma when combining only two nouns) and teriyaki sauce in with it. I'm not one to play with food so that intrigued me. What made me want to gag was when she drank a mouthful of it out of a 6oz container.

The mild hot sauce where I work is two thirds liquid margarine. What was the point of not having a bun? You just drank mayonnaise and butter like it was a soft drink. Sometimes I don't understand what makes people think that helps. Two whoppers with large fries and a large diet coke please!

P.S. Grammar Nazis are my friends. Correct anything you see that's wrong.

Biggest thing to work on: Word order with with the word whom (Who with? With whom?), the relationship between punctuation and quotation marks, identifying independent and dependent clauses and, by extension, when a semicolon is appropriate over a comma.

"Bread has way too much carbs, I'm not eating that!".

Grammar Nazis are my people. Punctuation can go outside of quotes, though. OP didn't need the period here, but punctuation goes outside of the quote if it's not a comma or period and if it affects the quote. For example:

Was she right when she said, "We are eating"?

The question mark goes outside the quote because to put it inside affects the quote i.e. it wasn't a question. In OP's case, the exclamation mark can be used within to quote because the quote was an exclamation and to end the sentence.

"Bread has way too many carbs, I'm not eating that"

should be:

"Bread has way too many carbs. I'm not eating that!"

or

"Bread has way too many carbs; I'm not eating that"

or

"Bread has way too many carbs [so] I'm not eating that"
